decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach toward the left lying cola bottle; open gripper and gradually pitch toward an overhead grasp.
Advance above the cola while pitching down; keep the right arm parked and preserve the current elbow branch.
Move the left wrist over the cola, approaching a downward grasp while maintaining clearance.
Align the downward fingers across the cola body, then lower cautiously to the estimated grasp height.
Close around the cola body and make a short verification lift; retention will be checked visually.
Lift the apparently captured cola and carry it left toward the bin with the gripper closed.
The cola remained on the table. Reopen and recenter over its shifted body for a deeper overhead grasp.
Center slightly right and descend around the cola body before closing; hold still to avoid pushing during closure.
Allow closure to finish, then lift vertically a short distance to verify a stable cola grasp.
Lift and translate the cola left without changing its grasp orientation; check that it follows the gripper.
Carry the retained cola toward the bin; start a small elbow-up right-arm approach toward the blue-and-white bottle.
Position the cola over the bin while centering the open right fingers around the blue bottle's lower body.
Release the cola over the bin, then withdraw. Close the right gripper around the blue-and-white bottle and begin a small test lift.
The cola is visible in the bin. Lift the blue bottle clear and prepare opposing, height-offset grippers for a central handover.
Raise the retained blue bottle above the pink bottle and turn the right gripper inward; bring the left hand toward the receiving pose.
Bring the bottle to the center for handover, with left fingers above the right grasp and both wrists staying on their own sides.
Lower the receiving fingers onto the exposed blue upper section and close, keeping the right grasp until the transfer is supported.
Release the donor hand, separate the wrists gently, and verify that the blue bottle remains with the closed left gripper.
Carry the blue bottle left toward the bin, and move the empty right wrist above the remaining rightmost lying bottle.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller right-wrist increments; continue the left-hand bin transfer.
Carry the blue bottle over the bin and gradually orient the right gripper downward for the lying white-green bottle.
Drop the blue bottle into the bin and withdraw the left wrist; continue the right overhead alignment.
Center the right wrist above the white-green bottle's body while finishing the downward orientation; stage the left hand for another transfer.
Finish the overhead alignment and descend toward the white-green bottle, keeping the left hand clear at the transfer side.
Lower the right fingers deeper around the lying bottle with a small lateral correction, then close while stationary.
The right descent met contact before reaching the target. Reopen, lift clear, and shift toward the bottle center rather than pressing down.
Correct the rightward offset seen in the wrist view with the fingers open, then approach the bottle again cautiously.
With the bottle now centered between the open fingers, descend a short distance and close for an overhead grasp.
Let the right grasp settle, then lift vertically to verify retention before attempting the handover.
Lift the retained tea bottle clear and begin rotating it upright while transporting it inward for handover.
Continue bringing the tea bottle upright and inward. Raise the left receiving gripper toward its exposed neck.
Turn the donor gripper inward while keeping the tea bottle upright; stage the left fingers above the donor grasp.
Complete the inward turn and place the tea bottle between the height-offset hands for the receiving grasp.
Close the left receiving gripper around the exposed upper bottle while the right hand continues supporting it.
The tea bottle slipped during the receiving closure. Separate and reopen the hands, preparing a left-side recovery after it settles.
Use smaller receiving-wrist rotations after the continuity rejection, moving clear and toward the fallen bottle without crossing arms.
Approach the settled tea bottle from above with the left hand, pitching down gradually; retract the empty right arm toward its own origin.
Keep clearance while finishing the left overhead orientation and recentering on the tea bottle; continue retracting the right hand.
Align the left pinch across the tea bottle and lower to a pregrasp height; ease the right hand back toward its origin.
Straighten the downward approach and lower the left gripper around the tea bottle; finish the right-arm return with small increments.
Make a final small alignment and close the left gripper on the tea bottle without lateral motion during closure.
Lift the tea bottle and start moving it toward the bin, preserving the closed grasp and current orientation.
Carry the retained tea bottle left and slightly rearward over the bin, keeping the grasp orientation fixed.
Release the tea bottle well inside the bin opening and lift the empty left hand clear.
Move the empty left hand toward the remaining pink bottle and turn the pinch direction across its length, keeping the wrist on the left side.
After the continuity interruption, approach the pink bottle with smaller translation and wrist-turn increments.
Approach the pink bottle from the left with a slightly inclined overhead grasp, keeping the left wrist on its own side.
Align the left fingers across the pink bottle's neck-side body and lower cautiously, without moving the wrist across the centerline.
Make a small final alignment around the pink bottle and close while stationary; the left wrist remains on its side.
Allow the pink-bottle grasp to settle, then make a short vertical lift to verify retention.
The pink bottle did not follow the lift. Reopen and incline the left fingers further toward its body for a deeper retry without crossing the wrist.
With the pink body centered between the fingers, lower farther for a secure pinch and close without lateral motion.
Hold closure to settle, then lift the pink bottle gently and check that it follows the left gripper.
Continue a small leftward verification lift with the gripper closed; retention of the pink bottle is still uncertain.
The pink bottle stayed on the table. Reopen and return to a lower body grasp, correcting for its small shift.
The pink body is centered in the wrist view. Lower another small amount to enclose its sides, then close without shifting.
Settle the deeper pinch, then lift vertically 24 mm while keeping the gripper fully commanded closed.
Lift the pink bottle farther and carry it left, keeping its deeper pinch unchanged and checking that it follows.
The pink bottle is following the left hand. Carry it toward the bin with the closed pinch and unchanged orientation.
Move the retained pink bottle fully over the bin opening before releasing it.
Open the left gripper to drop the pink bottle into the bin, pause for clearance, then begin withdrawing toward origin.
All four bottles are visible in the bin. Return the empty arms toward their original poses, maintaining the elbow-up branch.
Continue the smooth left-arm return toward origin with both grippers open and the right arm parked.
Ease the left arm close to its original pose with smaller increments; keep both grippers open.
